message.content: Tailscale Serve enables users to share a local server securely within their tailnet, which is a private network of devices managed by Tailscale [2]. It allows specific services or applications running on a local device to be accessible to other devices within the same tailnet. For example, users can expose a local web server, database, or API through the tailnet using configured HTTP(S) ports, path routing, or raw TCP connections [1]. The `tailscale serve` command is used to configure and manage these local services within the private network [2]. To share services beyond the tailnet, users must use the `tailscale funnel` command instead [2].

# tailscale serve: the commands that matter

Every tailscale serve command you will use, checked on Tailscale 1.102.4: foreground versus background, HTTPS ports, path routing, static files and raw TCP.

passages.heading: Turn one thing off, or reset everything
passages.text:
## Turn one thing off, or reset everything

The `off` form repeats the flags that created the handler. The target is optional:

```
sudo tailscale serve --https=443 --set-path=/api off
sudo tailscale serve --https=8443 off
sudo tailscale serve --tcp=5432 off
```
Name the wrong port or path and you remove nothing, or the wrong thing, which is why `status` comes first. To clear every handler on the node at once:

`sudo tailscale serve reset`
`reset` prints nothing. Run `status` afterwards and it reports `No serve config`. Reset replaces the whole serve config with an empty one, and Funnel listeners live in that same config, so they are cleared too. Re-add any public listener afterwards.

passages.heading: How do I remove a single serve handler without clearing the rest?
passages.text:
### How do I remove a single serve handler without clearing the rest?

Repeat the flags that created it and append `off`, for example `sudo tailscale serve --https=443 --set-path=/api off`. Run `sudo tailscale serve status` first to see the exact port and path. `sudo tailscale serve reset` clears every handler on the node instead, including Funnel.
